description: Post-country-first-AOR-mode and reviewer-hierarchy structural ceiling for Insight Hub 2 after browser-CI, dead-code hardening, React 19 state-map compatibility, OSHA database-persistence hardening, discovery-first occupational work, isolated official-source webviews, and the native reviewer intelligence transplant. The active application keeps one shell, three global CSS layers, reviewed page-level style blocks, lazy-loaded workspaces, and protected Hub 2 intelligence ownership routes. Injuries & Medical Conditions restores the Reviewer holographic injury-anatomy experience through a dedicated 24,000-point Three.js human-mesh projection while keeping Insight Hub 2 styling. Job Intelligence, Drug Checker, Clinical Calculators, and Standards Intelligence use a shared hierarchy-first visual system: primary action, dominant hero/result, supporting evidence, then interpretation/source boundaries. Drug Checker uses the real PubChem compound structure as the molecular hero with a dedicated transparent-canvas renderer and Insight Hub 2 aurora teal/cyan/blue/violet treatment. AOR Factors uses one MapTiler SDK vector-tile map with explicit Country and AOR selection modes. Country mode is the default and does not force a combatant command; AOR mode exposes command-wide geography and feeds. Country selection/search synchronizes State travel advisories, CDC Travelers' Health vaccine/medicine guidance and destination-listed infectious-disease context, WHO outbreak intelligence, GDACS hazards, USGS seismic activity, CrisisWatch conflict context, and environmental/human-performance factors. AOR mode shows command-wide WHO/GDACS/USGS intelligence. WHO Disease Outbreak News is fetched from the current WHO endpoint without unsupported query parameters and filtered locally. Country-level WHO, GDACS, and USGS displays never substitute unrelated command-wide events when the selected country has no match. CDC travel-health content is source-attributed and explicitly presented as general destination guidance rather than individualized medical advice or a disease-prevalence ranking. Duplicate files, generated artifacts, invalid coordinates, extra app shells, new unreachable frontend files, additional architecture candidates, and additional injected-style files remain prohibited unless this baseline is deliberately reviewed and updated. Job Intelligence deliberately adds one Neon persistence service, one dedicated profile API route, and one browser acceptance test; the reviewed repository file ceiling is 270 while all other structural ceilings remain unchanged. AOR operational-priority hardening deliberately adds two focused frontend modules: a versioned command assignment registry and a source-defined priority brief; the reviewed repository file ceiling is 272. Drug Checker live-intelligence hardening deliberately adds one dedicated backend route module; the reviewed repository file ceiling is 273. Clinical Calculators medical-risk hardening deliberately adds one focused browser acceptance test; the reviewed repository file ceiling is 274. Standards Intelligence deliberately replaces the required browser-owned standards data/rule module with one required API-owned standards registry/evaluator route, so the total repository file ceiling remains 274. AOR country-source resilience deliberately adds one backend route that owns strict country matching, WHO newest-first behavior, and GDACS country-search/global-feed fallback without unrelated substitutions; CDC destination resolution is hardened in the existing travel-health route. The reviewed repository file ceiling is therefore 275 while the duplicate, generated-artifact, reachability, shell, CSS, coordinate, and architecture-candidate ceilings remain unchanged. The entity-intelligence and occupational-hierarchy rebuild deliberately adds six focused modules: entity-context wrapping, entity-linked public intelligence, Industry Impact v2, Occupational Calculators v2, Job Intelligence v2, and exact O*NET code resolution. Compatibility aliases keep the superseded page modules present while routing users into the new consolidated experiences, raising the reviewed file ceiling to 281 and the transitional unreachable-frontend ceiling to 56; those legacy modules should be removed in a later cleanup once compatibility requirements are retired. Subsequent reviewed production work already present on main raised the actual repository tree to 287 files without increasing any duplicate, generated-artifact, shell, CSS, coordinate, architecture-candidate, or unreachable-frontend ceilings. The WarCosts integration deliberately adds three focused product modules: one API mirror/persistence route, one typed frontend client, and one native War & Defense Intelligence workspace. A fourth small API-server declaration restores Node fetch JSON compatibility for existing source adapters under the current TypeScript toolchain. The WarCosts second-pass completeness audit deliberately adds two more focused modules: one same-domain page-evidence crawler/persistence route and one native Site Evidence workspace, covering page-specific WarCosts facts that are not separately packaged in the 39 unique downloadable JSON files. The WarCosts feature-parity and ArcGIS pass deliberately adds five reachable frontend modules: a unified WarCosts subnavigation component, shared source-data utilities, native calculators, an ArcGIS 5.1 conflict/military-presence map, and the interactive tools workspace. The existing API app exposes the Render-provided ARCGIS_API_KEY only through a no-store WarCosts runtime-config endpoint while AOR remains isolated on MapTiler. A final specialized-tools module recreates the foreign-aid tax calculator, country military comparator, Strait of Hormuz impact calculator, and Iran-vs-Iraq comparison under the same single WarCosts sidebar workspace. The reviewed repository file ceiling is therefore 299; all other structural ceilings remain unchanged.
